claims.text: This tour will cover approximately 585 meters from Union Oyster House to Cheers Boston, showcasing Boston's rich seafood culture.
Explore the personal journeys of chefs and restaurateurs intertwined with time-honored seafood traditions as you delve into the vibrant tapestry of Boston's culinary heritage.

As you continue your tour, you will learn that Wilson visited Neptune Oyster during a challenging period at Neptune Oyster and that Cheers Boston officially embraced its pop culture legacy in 2002 at Cheers Boston.
As you step onto Union Street, the rich, savory aroma of fresh oysters greets you, drawing you toward the storied entrance of the Union Oyster House at numbers 41–43.
Established in 1826, the Union Oyster House holds the title of America's oldest continuously operating restaurant.
claims.evidence: The Union Oyster House, opened in 1826, is the oldest continuously operating restaurant in the United States.

claims.text: Nestled in a building originally constructed for Capen's Dry Goods in the early 1700s, this landmark retains an unmistakable sense of history.
The Union Oyster House is not just a relic but a living part of Boston culture where history and gastronomy converge.

The restaurant's patrons have included esteemed figures such as Calvin Coolidge, Franklin D. Roosevelt, Bill Clinton, and Barack Obama—each perhaps drawn by the promise of classic New England seafood served with a side of tradition.
In fact, Barack Obama's visit in 2010 caused quite a stir; the sitting president enjoyed the clam chowder, a decision that resonates with locals proud of their regional cuisine.
Today, the Union Oyster House is a cornerstone of Boston's Blackstone Block Historic District.
Open Sunday through Thursday from 11:00 am to 9:00 pm, and until 10:00 pm on Fridays and Saturdays, this iconic establishment invites you to savor classic dishes at prices under $30.
And while you might not leave with a presidential seal of approval, you'll certainly find a taste of Boston's enduring seafood tradition.
As you carry the flavor of this timeless experience with you, know that the next stop on our tour promises to take you further into the evolution of Boston's seafood delights.
The restaurant's tight-knit, 37-seat interior mirrors the intimate oyster bars of Paris, a direct nod to its founders' inspiration.
Jeff, who spent twelve years as a beverage manager at Todd English's Olives, brought his expertise to this intimate spot, transforming it into a pioneering force in Boston's dining scene.
Such dishes have become staples in Boston's culinary landscape, with Neptune Oyster frequently cited as a must-visit for seafood enthusiasts.
One notable story that highlights Neptune’s impact involves writer Korsha Wilson.
In a personal narrative, Wilson shared that she visited Neptune Oyster during a challenging period when both she and her partner had lost their jobs.
This story underscores Neptune's role beyond just a dining spot—it serves as a haven for those seeking comfort and connection through food.
In 2022, Food & Wine magazine named Neptune Oyster one of America's Best Oyster Bars, acknowledging its significant contribution to the culinary arts.
With its no-reservations policy, Neptune remains accessible to all who are willing to wait in line, eager to experience the flavors that have made it a beloved Boston institution.
As you enjoy the fresh seafood, consider the stories—like Wilson's—that each dish might tell.
The story of Cheers Boston begins in 1969, when and a partner transformed a basement storage space in the Hampshire House into the Bull & Finch Pub.
The Bull & Finch Pub officially embraced its pop culture legacy in 2002, renaming itself Cheers after a successful deal with CBS Studios, the show’s rights holder.

Unlike the seafood feasts you enjoyed at Union Oyster House and Neptune Oyster earlier on this tour, Cheers Boston offers a hearty menu of American staples, best washed down with a cold beer or a carefully crafted cocktail.
While you may not find Sam Malone pouring drinks behind the bar, the camaraderie and warmth that Cheers embodied on screen are palpable here.
Cheers operates from 11:00 to 22:00 daily, with the kitchen closing at 21:00.
